title: Tanzanian Sweet Potato Leaves
community: Enjoyed across Tanzania — another whole-plant vegetable
author: Mama Salima
desc: Tanzanian Matembele — sweet potato vine tips sautéed with onions, tomatoes, and garlic. The tender, slightly sweet greens from the same plant that produces Tanzania's beloved sweet potato — another zero-waste Tanzanian vegetable.
longDesc: Matembele (sweet potato leaves and vine tips) are harvested from the sweet potato plant while the tubers develop underground — providing a continuous supply of nutritious greens from a plant that also produces a significant root crop. The leaves are sweeter and more tender than most African greens.
ingredients: 400g sweet potato vine tips and leaves — washed and chopped
steps: Heat oil. Cook onions until golden.
Cover and cook 5—6 minutes until completely wilted.
chefTips: Only the young tender vine tips — mature stems are stringy.
Sweet potato leaves wilt faster than mchicha — check at 4 minutes.
commonMistakes: Using mature stems — tough and stringy.
cookingScience: Sweet potato leaves have a higher beta-carotene content than the tubers themselves — the green colour from chlorophyll accompanies exceptionally high provitamin A levels.
sustainabilityTips: Harvesting vine tips stimulates the plant to produce more leaves — and does not affect the underground tuber development.
culturalNote: Matembele is Tanzania's gift from the sweet potato plant — while the tubers provide starchy carbohydrate below ground, the leaves provide vitamins and minerals above. Nothing goes to waste.
